challengeFindings.title: A subagent commits its edit in a feature worktree whose tree also carries another feature's in-progress run, and `bkit tests changed` still lists nothing, so lint and typecheck never run on its files

A gaps-fix subagent commits its source fix, its first `steps finish` refuses a contradicted planned-test edit and writes a `build-takeover` row stamped with the post-fix `HEAD`, and `scan-diff --since-step` then measures from after the fix, exits 1 and sends the run to a needless Decision Pause

A debug run works in place on `dev` while another agent commits there (or `sync-dev` fast-forwards it), and `bkit tests changed` now lists every file those foreign commits touched, so the debug agent's gate fails on work it does not own and it is told every test must pass

Someone runs `scan-diff --since-step` by hand with a step name the run has no row for (a typo, or before `steps finish`), and it quietly measures from the run's last row, which is the step's own finish commit, and exits 1 "no source change" instead of refusing

Two commits land in the same second, the first holding any row stamped with that second (an `engine-call` or `engine-action` row), and `commitOfRow` finds the row by its second-precision `at` alone, so it returns the earlier commit and the base takes in the previous step's own commit

A by-hand `steps finish --field=uncommitted=true` on a committed step sets the new routing flag, and `stepBase` then returns the row's `parentSha`, so the next step's base includes that step's own commit

A person runs `bkit tests changed` by hand on `dev`, where the only in-progress run is another feature's abandoned run, and the default base silently becomes that run's last step-done commit, so the gate runs over every file changed on `dev` since then instead of the uncommitted files

challengeFindings.title: A build runs in a cloud runtime that adopts its session branch in place (`claude/...`, not `feat/{FID}`), the tree carries another feature's in-progress run from `dev`, a subagent commits its edit, and `bkit tests changed` still lists nothing, so lint and typecheck never run on its files

A collaborator pushes a branch named `feat/1-x/nested` (git accepts nested names and characters such as `;$(id)`), and `stepBase` takes everything after `feat/` as the FID with no slug allowlist, so `statusLocation` builds a path from it and a status file the branch name spells, in the main checkout or a nested log folder, sets the base of `bkit tests changed`
